turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - b3_htsteel_pareto_train.csv: 300 real steels, process/composition
    columns (Fe, Cr, Ni, Mo, Mn, C, Ti, Si, Nb, V, P, B, Al, Cu, W, S, Heat treatment
    step 1 temperature, Heat treatment step 1 time, Heat treatment step 1 cooling rate, Heat treatment step 2
    temperature, Heat treatment step 2 time, Heat treatment step 2 cooling rate, Heat treatment step 3
    temperature, Heat treatment step 3 time, Heat treatment step 3 cooling rate, Secondary treatment step 1
    temperature, Secondary treatment step 1 time, Secondary treatment step 2 temperature, Secondary treatment step 2
    time, Secondary treatment step 3 temperature, Secondary treatment step 3 time, Secondary treatment step 4
    temperature, Secondary treatment step 4 time, Thermal exposure temperature, Thermal exposure time) and
    the two measured objectives `yield strength (MPa)` and `elongation (%)`
    (both at room temperature).
  - b3_htsteel_pareto_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE steels whose objectives were
    NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and the same process/composition
    columns.

Select 5 candidates that jointly span the best trade-off between HIGH yield
strength (MPa) and HIGH elongation (%). Neither objective is given for the
pool. Your 5 picks are scored by the dominated hypervolume they span in the
normalized (yield strength (MPa), elongation (%)) plane, so a set of
mutually non-dominated candidates covering the frontier beats 5 candidates
that are all strong on one axis only.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit list of
candidate_ids, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
To select the 5 candidates that jointly span the best trade-off (Pareto frontier) between high yield strength (MPa) and high elongation (%), we can match the compositions and heat treatment (HT) / aging (AH) parameters of the pool candidates to the closest counterparts in the training data. 

Here is the step-by-step derivation for the 5 chosen candidates to cover the frontier from maximum elongation to maximum yield strength:

1. **Extreme Elongation, Low Yield Strength:**
   **`c086`** (`Fe~71.4, Cr~18.0, Ni~9.0, C~0.17`, HT1=1100°C, HT2=30°C)
   This is a classic austenitic stainless steel. In the training data, a nearly identical composition with slightly lower carbon (C=0.06) and HT1=1050°C achieves an outstanding **Elongation of 64%** and Yield Strength of 240 MPa. The higher carbon content and higher solutionizing temperature (1100°C) in `c086` will keep the carbon in solid solution, providing a slight boost to yield strength (estimated ~280 MPa) while maintaining extreme ductility (Elongation ~60-65%).

2. **High Elongation, Moderate Yield Strength:**
   **`c051`** (`Fe~62.4, Cr~20.5, Ni~13.5, Si~2.5`, HT1=1100°C, HT2=30°C)
   This candidate matches a training data point exactly in composition. The training counterpart processed at HT1=1150°C achieves a **Yield Strength of 375 MPa** and **Elongation of 53%**. The slightly lower solution annealing temperature of 1100°C for `c051` will yield very similar, highly balanced properties (estimated YS ~390 MPa, El ~50%).

3. **Balanced Yield Strength and Elongation:**
   **`c012`** (`Fe~64.9, Cr~11.25, Ni~19.5, Ti~2.9`, HT1=1175°C, AH1=750°C)
   This is an A286-type precipitation-hardening alloy. Its exact compositional match in the training data, aged at 700°C, achieves a **Yield Strength of 700 MPa** and **Elongation of 34%**. `c012` is aged at a slightly higher temperature (750°C), which will slightly overage the $\gamma'$ / $\eta$ precipitates, ensuring the elongation remains excellent (~35%) while keeping the yield strength highly competitive (~650-700 MPa).

4. **High Yield Strength, Moderate Elongation:**
   **`c098`** (`Fe~96.4, Cr~1.65, C~0.255`, HT1=950°C, HT2=620°C, Aging=450°C for 6000 mins)
   This low-alloy martensitic steel matches a training sample that was aged at 450°C for 3000 mins, which achieved a **Yield Strength of 940 MPa** and **Elongation of 18%**. The extended aging time (6000 mins) at the same low tempering temperature will push the secondary hardening slightly further, reliably securing a Yield Strength of ~960 MPa while preserving the ~18% elongation.

5. **Extreme Yield Strength, Low-Moderate Elongation:**
   **`c053`** (`Fe~83.7, Cr~11.25, Ni~1.65, C~0.13`, HT1=1000°C, HT2=450°C)
   This candidate is a martensitic stainless steel. It is a near-perfect match to a training sample (`Fe~82.95, Cr~11.25, Ni~1.65, C~0.13`) that was quenched and tempered at the exact same temperatures (HT1=1000°C, HT2=450°C). The training sample achieved a massive **Yield Strength of 1380 MPa** with a very respectable **Elongation of 15%**. This anchors the extreme high-strength end of our Pareto front.

These 5 candidates are mutually non-dominated and perfectly spaced to maximize the hypervolume of the trade-off frontier.

Final: c086, c051, c012, c098, c053
